canonical_topic: Wake effect and wind farm layout
definition: When one turbine sits downwind of another, it receives turbulent, disrupted airflow rather than clean wind, which lowers its output and increases mechanical stress.
core_idea: The upwind turbine disturbs the wind flow reaching downwind turbines, so wind farm layouts are typically arranged in lines or otherwise spaced out to minimize this interference between units.
key_points: A downwind turbine experiences chaotic/disrupted airflow caused by the turbine upwind of it.
Wind farms are commonly organized in lines or spread out specifically to reduce this inter-turbine disruption.
relationships: Related to overall wind farm capacity factor and turbine spacing decisions
trading_implications: Physical layout constraints limit how densely a wind farm can be built on a given parcel, which caps nameplate capacity per unit of land.
